stories.title: Jerusalem schools strike after Israel enforces curriculum and bans teachers
stories.summary: Private and Christian schools in East Jerusalem have declared an open-ended strike, protesting sudden Israeli permit blockades for West Bank educators and a systematic push to replace the Palestinian curriculum. The academic year in occupied East Jerusalem began on Tuesday with an open-ended strike by teachers at private and Christian schools after Israeli meddling in students’ curriculum. All new first and seventh-grade classes at East Jerusalem’s Palestinian-majority municipal schools have been told to exclusively use the Israeli curriculum this year. Entry permits for West Bank teachers to teach in East Jerusalem schools have also been blocked by Israel, according to Haaretz. It means that one-in-three Palestinian students in occupied East Jerusalem, more than 45,000 in total, will be enrolled in the Israeli educational programme, a nearly fourfold increase over six years ago. Jerusalem Governorate spokesman Marouf al-Rifai described the forced integration of Israeli curriculum into Palestinian schools as a cultural and educational crime. “The adherence of Jerusalem’s people, teachers, and students to the Palestinian curriculum is not merely an adherence to a textbook, but rather a defense of memory, identity, history, and the right to determine the national narrative,” he said in a statement on Facebook. Israeli forces recently seized educational compounds formerly operated by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA, in the Shu’fat refugee camp and Kafr Aqab, to be replaced with Israeli-administered facilities. Hamas official Haroun Nasser el-Din issued a statement saying that “the school, the book, and awareness are basic pillars in the battle of Jerusalem”. East Jerusalem and the West Bank have been illegally occupied by Israel since 1967. “The Palestinian identity in Jerusalem is deeper than to be erased by imposed curricula or the occupation’s procedures and its arrogant policies,” he added. Palestinian schools in East Jerusalem have already suffered a severe staffing shortage due to Israel effectively blocking teachers from the West Bank from reaching the city’s schools.

stories.title: Bank of Russia raises dollar exchange rate to 86.75 rubles for September 2
stories.summary: The official euro exchange rate has been raised by 2.74 kopecks to 100.5988 rubles
article_sentences: The Bank of Russia has set the official dollar exchange rate at 86.753 rubles for September 2, 2026, which is 37.37 kopecks higher than the previous indicator.
The official euro exchange rate has been raised by 2.74 kopecks to 100.5988 rubles.
The official yuan exchange rate has been raised by 3.9 kopecks to 12.897 rubles.
